evidence.note: Step 3.1 omitted the inclusion isomorphism from H_n(N_p,N_p\{p};Z_2) to H_n(Y,Y\{p};Z_2). The compact neighborhood N_p contains an open neighborhood of p, so closure(Y\N_p) avoids p and lies in the open subspace Y\{p}. The published excision theorem therefore applies exactly to this inclusion. The certificate and global point-local chains coincide, so the nonzero class transports. Added F6, the direct mathematical dependency, exact contract citation and proof derivation; confidence 1. This is a short nonfatal inference omission, not a false sufficient-construction claim.
